module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 35

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/35](https://www.erdosproblems.com/35)
- [Er56] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in additive number theory*. Colloque sur la Théorie des
  Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
- [Er36c] Erdős, P., *On the arithmetical density of the sum of two sequences, one of which forms
  a basis for the integers*. Acta. Arith. (1936), 201-207.
- [Pl70] Plünnecke, H., *Eine zahlentheoretische Anwendung der Graphentheorie*. J. Reine. Angew.
  Math. (1970), 171-183.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set Pointwise

namespace Erdos35

open scoped Classical in
/--
Let $B\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an additive basis of order $k$ with $0\in B$. Is it true that for
every $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ we have
$$d_s(A+B)\geq \alpha+\frac{\alpha(1-\alpha)}{k},$$
where $\alpha=d_s(A)$ and
$$d_s(A) = \inf \frac{\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N}$$
is the Schnirelmann density?

Erdős [Er36c] proved this is true with $k$ replaced by $2k$ in the denominator (in a stronger form
that only considers $A\cup (A+b)$ for some $b\in B$, see [38](https://www.erdosproblems.com/38)).

Ruzsa has observed that this follows immediately from the stronger fact proved by Plünnecke
[Pl70] that (under the same assumptions)
$$d_S(A+B)\geq \alpha^{1-1/k}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos35.lean#L1738"]
theorem erdos_35 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (B : Set ℕ) (k : ℕ), 0 ∈ B → B.IsAddBasisOfOrder k →
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, schnirelmannDensity A +
      schnirelmannDensity A * (1 - schnirelmannDensity A) / k ≤ schnirelmannDensity (A + B) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Plünnecke [Pl70] proved that if $B\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is an additive basis of order $k$ with
$0\in B$ then $d_S(A+B)\geq d_s(A)^{1-1/k}$ for every $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_35.variants.plunnecke (B : Set ℕ) (k : ℕ) (h0 : 0 ∈ B) (hB : B.IsAddBasisOfOrder k)
    (A : Set ℕ) :
    schnirelmannDensity A ^ (1 - (k : ℝ)⁻¹) ≤ schnirelmannDensity (A + B) := by
  sorry

end Erdos35

findings.description: The positive-density hypothesis from Plünnecke's theorem is missing. The declaration permits B = Set.univ, k = 1, and A = ∅. Both basis hypotheses hold, but the conclusion reduces to 1 ≤ 0: the exponent is zero, Real.rpow defines 0^0 = 1, and the empty sumset has Schnirelmann density zero. This counterexample, and the negation of the universally quantified declaration, were proved in Lean without sorryAx. Merely requiring A to be nonempty or infinite would not fix it: A = Set.Ici 2 is another verified counterexample.
findings.source_evidence: Plünnecke, Eine zahlentheoretische Anwendung der Graphentheorie (1970), Satz 1.2, p. 172, explicitly takes a positive density parameter in (0,1] and sets A whose Schnirelmann density is at least that parameter. See https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN243919689_0243/PPN243919689_0243.pdf, PDF p. 177. The remark at https://www.erdosproblems.com/35 quotes the power bound without this endpoint qualification.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `(hA : 0 < schnirelmannDensity A)` after `(A : Set ℕ)`, matching the primary theorem. Qualify the power-bound remarks in both docstrings accordingly. The main polynomial-bound theorem needs no such restriction, since its zero-density case is trivial.

findings.description: The module bibliography gives the wrong page range for [Er36c]: 201–207 rather than 197–200. This is a reference slip, not a defect in the main inequality.
findings.source_evidence: The original article at https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1936-06.pdf occupies pp. 197–200. Erdős [Er56], p. 135, footnote (11), gives 'Acta arithm., 1 (1936), 197–200' (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1956-17.pdf); Plünnecke [Pl70], p. 183, reference [1], independently gives the same pagination.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the [Er36c] citation to Acta Arith. 1 (1936), 197–200.

reformulations.difference: The basis hypothesis uses exactly k summands through IsAddBasisOfOrder, whereas Erdős [Er56], p. 135, defines a basis using k or fewer summands.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the explicit hypothesis 0 ∈ B, any representation with at most k summands can be padded with zeros to use exactly k; the converse is immediate. Both the equivalence of the basis predicates and the equivalence of the resulting universally quantified polynomial-bound statements were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/35 (HTML read via https://r.jina.ai/http://www.erdosproblems.com/35; exact LaTeX via https://r.jina.ai/http://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/35)
Local review guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md; all eight provided not-misformalization cases; past-misformalization examples pr04211, pr00637, pr01518, and pr04028.
review.notes: The main theorem faithfully matches the website's affirmative question and current PROVED (LEAN) status. Its cited external proof compiled successfully and uses only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound; its basis predicate was also checked against the repository's. Scratch checks establish that order zero is impossible, verify the main theorem's order-one and density endpoints, and certify both counterexamples and the basis reformulation without sorryAx. No changes were made to the reviewed file.

demonstrated.claim: The declaration is false: B = Set.univ, k = 1, and A = ∅ satisfy its hypotheses but reduce its conclusion to 1 ≤ 0.

submission.summary: Created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean with a short disproof of the declaration's exact type using type_of%. Compilation succeeds without warnings or errors, and the proof's axioms do not include sorryAx.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«35»

/-! A boundary counterexample to the Plünnecke variant of Erdős problem 35. -/

open scoped Pointwise Classical

-- Erdos35.erdos_35.variants.plunnecke is false: B = ℕ, k = 1, A = ∅ satisfy
-- its hypotheses, but its conclusion is 0^0 ≤ 0, i.e. 1 ≤ 0.
theorem plunnecke_counterexample :
    ¬ (type_of% @Erdos35.erdos_35.variants.plunnecke) := by
  intro h
  have hbad := h (Set.univ : Set ℕ) 1 (by simp) (by simp) (∅ : Set ℕ)
  norm_num at hbad

#print axioms plunnecke_counterexample

submission.summary: Added the positive Schnirelmann-density hypothesis to the Plünnecke variant and qualified both associated docstrings. Left the main polynomial-bound statement unchanged. Also corrected the reported [Er36c] page-range typo to 197–200. The edited file compiles with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
